records.title: Menstrual history in altitude chamber trainees.
records.locator: Methods and Materials, pp. 616–617, and Table I, p. 617
records.evidence_note: The Methods explicitly give two DCS cases in 510 usable survey responses. Both were identified from their unit Chamber Reactor/Treatment Reports and excluded before the main analysis. The 508 analyzed records are selected noncases. The survey was voluntary and anonymous after the chamber flight, with authors estimating participation by approximately one-third of women trained. The response denominator supplies neither a complete risk set for women trainees nor exposure totals for staff.

observations.group: Female trainees with usable questionnaires before exclusion for DCS
observations.note: 541 responses received, 31 unusable, two cases then excluded to leave 508 noncases. The sampling frame, missing outcome data for nonrespondents, repeat participation, exact calendar and follow-up intervals are unverified.

records.title: Relationship of menstrual history to altitude chamber decompression sickness.
records.locator: Methods, Results, and Table I, pp. 657–658
records.evidence_note: Treated female patient records cover 1978–1988. Four of 85 records with date-of-last-menses data were excluded. All 19 Type II cases in the 81-record subset had neurological symptoms. The cycle exposure distribution was assumed for comparison and was not measured. The study provides no role-specific risks, no exposed denominator, and no basis to join its cases to the later voluntary survey.

observations.group: Female treated cases selected for menstrual history analysis
observations.note: The 81 are a subset of available treated patient records, not all exposed women. Duty positions are unreported. See links to overlapping USAFSAM treatment files.

records.title: Decompression sickness: USAF experience 1970-80.
records.evidence_note: The 58 reported cases are attributed to actual aircraft. The 36-case subgroup includes intentional depressurization or unpressurized flight. The use of trainer aircraft in some cases does not establish chamber training. No chamber staff or trainee risk set is reported.

note: Verified the baseline respondents, follow-up selection and distinction between reported symptom histories and radiographic findings.

records.title: X-ray survey for bone changes in low-pressure chamber operators
records.locator: Methods and Results, pp. 760–762, especially Table I, p. 761
records.evidence_note: Self-reported dysbarism history includes aerosinusitis. Chamber and aircraft hours are both described. Event exposure and case units cannot be aligned to a chamber person-exposure denominator. The authors’ May 1960 conference manuscript presents the same data.

observations.group: USAF chamber operators in the 1958 survey
observations.note: Retrospective occupational history. There were 341 reported episodes including one aerosinusitis. Mixed exposure histories and absent event-specific attribution limit interpretation.

records.title: X-ray survey for bone changes in low-pressure chamber operators
records.evidence_note: The UTMB typescript identifies the May 1960 AsMA meeting in Miami. Its Results give the same 283/579 respondents with prior dysbarism and 341 reported episodes as the September journal publication. Keep one quantitative survey extraction.

records.title: Seven year follow-up x-ray survey for bone changes in low pressure chamber operators.
records.locator: Methods and Results, pp. 417–420, especially Tables I–IV
records.evidence_note: The 623 baseline sets on file included 44 too late for the 1960 paper. The 164 respondents were traceable active-duty members of the baseline collection. The 571 episodes are quantified cumulative self-reports. Table III excludes frequent symptoms reported without counts. The article describes aircraft and diving histories alongside chamber exposure. It reports two compatible imaging lesions, with uncertain onset and causation. One was already visible on a baseline film and the other lacked complete baseline imaging.

observations.group: Responding Air Force chamber operators in the 1966 follow-up
observations.note: Cumulative history in selected respondents. Case events are not matched to chamber hours or incident calendar window. The earlier survey and this follow-up share participants.

observations.group: Responding Air Force chamber operators in the 1966 follow-up
observations.note: Potential radiographic sequelae with uncertain causation. This endpoint is distinct from symptomatic DCS.

records.title: Preliminary investigation of bone change as a result of exposure to reduced atmospheric pressure.
records.locator: Methods and Results, p. 188, and Table I and historical addendum, p. 189
records.evidence_note: This report describes USN inside observers surveyed in 1954–1955. All seven with positive findings were male hospital corpsmen. The authors describe the findings as asymptomatic and note the original reading may have included normal bone islands. The paper discusses the collection of symptoms by questionnaire but gives no symptomatic DCS numerator. The 1970 addendum explicitly identifies the findings as those presented in Chicago in 1956.

observations.group: USN inside observers with completed imaging
observations.locator: Results, p. 188, Table I and addendum, p. 189
observations.note: Seven affected people and 11 radiographic findings. Findings include possible normal variants and provide no symptomatic DCS estimate.

records.title: U.S. Air Force experience in hypobaric osteonecrosis
records.evidence_note: The workshop paper discusses the same long-bone studies and repeats two lesions in 164 follow-up respondents. Its 44 respondents with no history of DCS differ from 57 in the primary Table II. The discrepancy is unresolved and the workshop is not an additional independent survey.

note: Verified citations for the Rudge conference paper, earlier Coburn presentation and a USAFSAM residency research paper.

records.title: Relationship of menstrual history to altitude chamber decompression sickness
records.evidence_note: The NASA index identifies a four-page contribution to the August 1990 AGARD proceedings. The index abstract reports the same 81 eligible records and 1978–1988 period as the full journal paper, which identifies the Tours presentation. The proceedings paper itself was not retrieved.

records.title: Preliminary investigation of bone changes as a result of exposure to reduced atmospheric pressure
records.locator: Hodgson et al. 1968, reference 4, and Coburn 1970, historical addendum, p. 189
records.evidence_note: Hodgson cites Journal of Aviation Medicine 27:163. Coburn identifies his 1970 paper as a précis of the 1956 Chicago presentation and says the original paper had not been published in full. The separately cited 1956 item was not retrieved.

records.title: Neurologic decompression sickness: A study of 63 non-fatal reactions occurring in USAF altitude chambers from 1951 through 1965
records.evidence_note: The bibliography describes this as a residency research paper from USAFSAM, Brooks AFB. The original report is unavailable. Comparability and case overlap with the C. A. Berry 1950–1955 surveillance are unverified.
